## Context / Problem

Most plan-review criteria have no eval fixture, so a rubric edit ships with no behavioral
oracle. The material is committed and free to read: manifest
`docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/replay/corpus-2026-08-30.manifest.json` records 6,482
sidecar rows with `verified_count` 6,202, and `plan_replay/corpus.py` reconstructs each
row's at-review plan text (`corpus.py:270-288`).

Mining it is not a dump: the corpus records what the reviewer said, not what was true, and
two hazards make naive selection wrong. Reviewer noise — 551 consecutive review pairs over
byte-identical material flipped verdict 208 times, so a fixture built from one observation
flips under that same noise. Prompt vintage — rubrics were rewritten repeatedly inside the
corpus window and `plan_review_verifier.md` last changed 2026-08-11, so a finding from a
retired rubric does not describe today's criterion. Nothing existing cohorts by vintage:
`regver` (`manifest.py:139-185`) hashes routing and criterion ids but not rubric bytes, and
`verified_at_sha` is read by no code under `src/rebar/llm/evals/`.

## Approach

An offline miner emitting CANDIDATE fixture specs to a working directory for the sibling
admission runner. It writes nothing into `.rebar/evals/` and issues no model call.

**Prior art.** Weak-supervision label mining (the Snorkel line) is the established pattern;
a hand-coded conjunction is used because the signals are few and fixed and an opaque learned
weighting would be unauditable in a merge-blocking gate. In-tree
`sampling.stratified_sample` targets replay sampling, not fixture emission.

**Vintage gate.** A review is eligible for criterion C only when `review_event_ts`
(`corpus.py:273`) postdates the last `origin/main` commit touching C's resolved prompt file.
Resolution follows the gate's own order: a project `.rebar/prompts/<prompt-id>.md` override
when present, else the packaged `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/<prompt-id>.md`. A criterion whose
resolved file has no committed history — a `project.`-prefixed overlay criterion, or a
brand-new rubric — FAILS the gate and is skipped, since no review can postdate a commit that
does not exist. A signal derived from the stored Pass-2 answer
vector additionally requires postdating the last commit to `plan_review_verifier.md`.

**Signals**, all offline and independent of the reviewer's own verdict:
- *Reproduction consensus* — the criterion fired, or stayed silent, consistently across two
  or more reviews with equal `material_fingerprint`. The only signal valid in the no-fire
  direction.
- *Author response* — `finding_survival == "resolved_by_author"` (`labels.py:158-171`), the
  only per-finding label the labels module produces. Fire direction only.
- *Escaped defect, positive use only* — a ticket that passed review then took a
  `plan_defect` close or an inbound `caused_by` link (`labels.py:70-73`) is a must-fire
  candidate. Its absence never evidences correct silence, so `clean_close` (`labels.py:43`)
  is excluded as a no-fire source.

**Tiered admission bar.** A FIRE candidate is BLOCKING only when all four hold: reproduction
consensus, author-response corroboration, `abs(decision_margin)` (`sidecar.py:344-367`) at or
above the constant `MIN_MARGIN = 0.15`, and the vintage gate.
The margin and author-response conjuncts are per-finding and exist only in the fire
direction, so a NO-FIRE candidate reaches at most ADVISORY, on reproduction consensus plus
the vintage gate. Any single signal plus the vintage gate proposes ADVISORY. The margin
constant drops findings close enough to `block_threshold` that a small perturbation flips
them — the population that makes a fixture flaky.

**Emitted shape and balance guarantee.** Per criterion at most 8 cases, targeting 4
`expect: finding` and 4 `expect: pass`, plus a non-empty `gold_set` (`eval.py:265-267`). A
criterion that cannot produce at least one case on EACH side of the axis, or no `gold_set`,
emits NO file and is counted `skipped-unbalanced`, so a one-sided dataset never reaches the
balance rule at `eval.py:252-255`. The sibling loop counts `skipped-unbalanced` as a failed
attempt, so a persistently unbalanced criterion is recorded by that child's
`unreliable-criterion:` breaker rather than vanishing.

**Output lifecycle and skip list.** Each run writes a fresh temporary tree and atomically
replaces the working directory, so no file survives for a criterion that becomes skipped or
specced. A criterion with an open `unreliable-criterion: <criterion-id>` ticket is skipped.

## Scope

A new module under `src/rebar/llm/evals/` holding the miner and its selection predicates,
consuming `plan_replay/corpus.py` and `plan_replay/labels.py`. It covers only criteria
`criteria.effective_routing('.', gate_key='plan_review')` reports having no spec under
`.rebar/evals/` or `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/`.

## Non-goals

- Writing into `.rebar/evals/` or admitting a candidate; the admission runner owns both.
- Any model call.
- Mining a criterion that already has a spec: `eval.py:69-78` resolves a project spec as a
  replacement, so a mined file would delete the packaged cases.
- Per-finding true/false-positive labelling or human adjudication.

## Testing

Unit tests over the selection predicates on synthetic corpus rows, plus one integration test
over the real committed corpus with no model configured. Every assertion is deterministic
because no model is involved.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A review timestamped before its criterion's resolved prompt commit is excluded, and an
      otherwise-identical later one is included; verified by `pytest` asserting the candidate
      set holds the second row's id and not the first's.
- [ ] A criterion whose resolved prompt file has no committed history is skipped; verified by
      `pytest` asserting a `project.`-prefixed criterion is absent from the candidate set.
- [ ] A fixture whose only no-fire signal is a clean close produces zero must-not-fire
      candidates; verified by `pytest` asserting an empty `expect: pass` case list.
- [ ] A ticket that passed review and later took a `plan_defect` close produces an
      `expect: finding` candidate; verified by `pytest` over a synthetic escaped-defect row.
- [ ] Each blocking conjunct, removed one at a time from a fire candidate, downgrades it to
      `advisory`, and the all-present case yields `blocking`; verified by parameterized
      `pytest` over the emitted tier string.
- [ ] A no-fire candidate never reaches `blocking`; verified by `pytest` asserting the tier
      is `advisory` for a no-fire candidate holding reproduction consensus.
- [ ] A criterion lacking any `expect: finding` case, or any `expect: pass` case, or a
      `gold_set`, emits no file and is counted as `skipped-unbalanced`; verified by `pytest`
      asserting no file exists for it and that the reported count names it.
- [ ] Every emitted spec returns zero errors from `validate_eval_spec(spec, strict=True)` and
      carries at most 8 cases; verified by `pytest` invoking the real validator per file.
- [ ] A criterion with an open `unreliable-criterion: <id>` ticket is absent from the emitted
      candidate set; verified by `pytest` with a stubbed ticket listing.
- [ ] Two consecutive real runs over the committed corpus emit byte-identical output;
      verified by `diff -r` of the two output trees exiting 0.
- [ ] A file emitted by a previous run for a criterion that becomes skipped does not survive
      the next run; verified by `pytest` asserting the path is absent after the second run.
- [ ] The miner completes with the repository's network guard active; verified by `pytest`
      running it under that guard.

## Definition of Done

`make lint`, `make typecheck` and `make test` pass; the real-corpus run completes; the diff
touches nothing under `.rebar/evals/` or `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/`.

## Budget

**$0.** Mining is a pure function of the corpus and git metadata.
